relevance_note: One cohort patient (case 20) has Alexander disease with a GFAP variant: Table 2 row '| 20 | Alexander disease' and Table 3 lists GFAP c.250A>T p.Ile84Phe for proband 20.
method_note: Panel-sequencing cohort of 49 leukoencephalopathy patients; only case 20 (Alexander disease, GFAP) is in scope; the other 19 diagnosed patients have variants in other genes and the remaining 29 had no diagnosis, so they get no rows. Label: Table 2 'Case' and Table 3 'Probands' columns hold bare numbers and the text never names this patient, so the label is 'Table 2 #20'. Spans were cut from the paper text by a small script (the paper prints thin spaces around '>' in variants) and checked by hand against the Table 2 and Table 3 rows. Age 0.8 is from the 'Sex, age (years)' column without saying which age it is (recorded as age at last evaluation, uncertain). HC '46.5(9M)' is printed without an interpretation and was not recorded as macrocephaly. 'EMG: normal', 'VEP: normal' and 'BAEP: normal' are whole investigations, recorded as excluded 'abnormal EMG/VEP/BAEP' without anything more specific. 'periventricular' white-matter signal is not described as a rim, so periventricular rim stays not reported. De novo is from the Table 3 'de novo/inherited' column together with the statement that parents of the probands were validated by Sanger sequencing; the paper does not separately print that both parents were negative for this variant. Pathogenicity comes from the Table 2 title ('patients with pathogenic mutations'), a named group that includes case 20; HGMD status 'Unreported' and in-silico predictions (SIFT, MutationTaster, PolyPhen-2) are not functional evidence and were not recorded as such. cites_prior_report_of_same_patients is null: the paper cites its earlier NDUFAF1 report but does not say any patient was described before, and this does not concern case 20. No contradictions found.
